newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close slightly higher.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Monday but the market remained cautious about the 1997 budget package, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 172.17
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 162.4
Volume was moderate at 140 million shekels with almost all the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.

"The response to the (November) consumer price figure was positive, but investors remain cautious as they await approval of the 1997 budget. The market has reached a ceiling and it will stabilize at its current level," said Roy Meir at Simodan.

The November consumer price index, announced on Sunday, was 0.6 percent, down from 0.8 percent in October. Meanwhile, the Treasury hopes to present to parliament a second round of budget cuts for 1997 later this week. The second round of cuts will bring the total planned reduction in the 1997 budget to 6.1 billion shekels.
In addition, the Treasury plans to raise 600 million shekels in new, non-tax income.
"The market also rose today because big institutional investors have increased liquidity and are trying to show improved results before the end-of-the-year," Meir added.
Traders noted that CPI-linked short bonds closed slightly lower while medium and long bonds rose mildly on low volume.

"Unlinked bonds continue to be the focus of activity but with minimal rises. The CPI was within expectations and the reaction was very moderate," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
Traders said Makams also rose in response to the inflation figure.
Dollar-linked bonds closed higher but traders said trading was again thin.
NOTE: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
